transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Rivera. Thank you for meeting with me. I have some important things to tell you about your treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it is not. I am very sorry to tell you that we made a mistake with your chemotherapy dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When we give the medicine, we calculate the amount based on your weight. We used your weight from a few months ago. But you have lost a lot of weight since then. Because of that, you received more medicine than you should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I feel very sick today. Is that why?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it is likely because of the extra medicine. I want to be very clear: this was my fault. I did not check your current weight before the dose was given. I am deeply sorry for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... I don't know. Will this make me more sick? I cannot go to the police or... I don't have papers. Will this change how you treat me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please know that your status does not change your right to safe care. We are here to help you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just worried that if there is a problem, maybe I should not be here. I don't want to cause trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are not causing trouble. I am the one who made the mistake. I take full responsibility for this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very scared. I don't like the way my stomach feels.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are feeling anxious.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, and I think maybe—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, so we need to look at the blood tests. We have to make sure your white blood cells are okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to say that I was thinking about my kids and—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go over the plan quickly because I have other patients to see. We are going to do a blood draw every morning for the next three days. That is your part, you just need to come to the lab at eight o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Eight o'clock. Okay. But what about the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have stopped the current cycle. We will wait five days before we start again, and I will personally weigh you right before the next dose to make sure the number is correct. Does that make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I think so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just to be sure I explained it well, can you tell me what happened with the dose?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You used the old weight. Too much medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring you closely. We will check your labs tomorrow morning, and I will come back to see you at ten to tell you the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still very worried about my status.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focused on your health right now. Let's wrap this up so the nurse can check your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see you tomorrow at ten.

H.justification: Resident interrupts the patient multiple times during emotional bids (regarding kids and status) and uses rushing language ('go over the plan quickly', 'wrap this up').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once via teach-back.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'deeply sorry') and took full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: Resident named one emotion ('anxious') but otherwise met emotional bids regarding the patient's children and legal status with factual redirection.

T.justification: Resident provided specific steps (blood draws, 5-day wait), timelines (8am, tomorrow at 10), the patient's role (come to the lab), and a prevention strategy (personally weighing the patient).
